words.gloss: adversity or the opposite of good

literal: When good fortune occurs, those who experience it as good things; when adversity occurs, experiencing distress, why?
translation: Why should those who gladly accept prosperity as a good thing when it comes, grieve and suffer distress when adversity comes?
modern: நன்மை வரும்போது அதனை நல்லதாக ஏற்றுக்கொள்பவர்கள், தீமை வரும்போது மட்டும் துன்பப்பட்டு வருந்துவது ஏன்?
explanation: This couplet points out the inconsistency in how people respond to the inevitable cycles of destiny. When good fortune (நன்று) arrives, people readily welcome and enjoy it as something natural and good (நல்லவா காண்பவர்). However, when the opposite—misfortune or adversity (அன்று)—strikes, they fall into deep grief and distress (அல்லல் படுவது). The poet asks 'why' (எவன்) they do this, suggesting that since both joy and sorrow are governed by the same law of destiny, one should maintain equanimity and accept both with an equal mind.
